subject: Inference VPN & Peering validation — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Inference VPN & Peering validation — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment for the performance qualification on the Private/VPC deployment.

Summary of requirements we heard on the call:
- Latency SLO: p95 inference token latency target ~ < 75ms for streaming endpoints (typical sequence lengths 128–512).
- Throughput: baseline 150 tokens/sec sustained per model replica during peak daytime windows; expected burst to 600 tokens/sec for 60s windows.
- Concurrency: up to 80 simultaneous streaming sessions for the pilot (scale to 300 in production).
- Streaming behavior: client expects chunked server-sent events with <100ms inter-chunk delay for interactive UX.
- Network constraints: traffic will traverse a site-to-site VPN today, with peering and dedicated egress IPs being evaluated next week.

Immediate asks from Redwood to ACME to validate feasibility:
1) Network diagram (egress points, VPN concentrator throughput, any intermediate firewall/CDN). You mentioned you would share this — thanks.
2) Prioritized traceroute/latency samples from an app host in ACME’s VPC to our test egress IPs (we shared two public egress candidates on the call). If possible include packet loss and MTU checks.
3) Approx VPN throughput (Mbps) and whether session-based concurrency caps exist on the VPN concentrator.
4) Expected data egress policy (will ACME require HTTP proxy or TLS interception?), and whether there are mandatory outbound proxy ports.

Proposed Redwood deliverables and timeline:
- By EOD Tue (2027-06-15): Redwood will provide a short preflight checklist and a targeted set of network tests (iperf/traceroute/soak test) + a small perf-run playbook for the pilot.
- Week of 6/21: On-prem/VPC PoC slot — 4-hour window to run an initial load test and streaming verification from your VPC to our test pool.
- Post-PoC: We'll share a short A/R report including measured p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and recommendations (batching, KV-cache, suggested concurrency caps).

Next concrete step: Alice — can you upload the network diagram and confirm the VPN concentrator model and throughput by EOB Monday (2027-06-14)? We’ll email the test egress IPs and the preflight script once we have that.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Inference VPN & Peering validation — post-call recap and next steps

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. 

I've attached our current network diagram (acme-network-diagram.pdf) and a short requirements sheet (acme-requirements-sheet.xlsx). A few notes from NetOps: 
- VPN concentrator: F5 BIG-IP APM, dual-head, site-to-site; aggregate throughput currently ~2 Gbps. No per-session hard cap configured but there are TLS inspection appliances in path that may add ~3–5ms of processing at peak.
- Egress: we currently NAT at two egress IPs per region; we can allocate dedicated egress IPs for Redwood PoC if needed.
- Proxy: outbound TLS passthrough expected (no interception) but we do enforce an outbound HTTP proxy on port 8080 for non-TLS traffic.

We will run a traceroute from an application host to the egress candidates you sent and return the logs by EOD Tue (2027-06-15).

Next steps from our side:
- NetOps will confirm whether we can schedule the PoC window during week of 6/21 and will loop in our security/compliance reviewer.

--
Alice Monroe
Director, Cloud Platforms | Acme Health
alice.monroe@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-6789

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf, acme-requirements-sheet.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference VPN & Peering validation — post-call recap and next steps

Appreciate the diagram and the notes, Alice — that's exactly what we needed. A couple of follow-ups based on your NetOps answers: 

1) TLS inspection note — the added 3–5ms is workable but we need to quantify variance under load. We'll include a small p95/p99 variance check in the preflight to measure if spikes push p95 beyond 75ms.
2) Dedicated egress IPs: yes please — having fixed egress IPs will simplify NAT traversal and firewall rules for the PoC. Please confirm the two IPs when available.
3) PoC window: we recommend a preflight test (iperf + traceroute + small streaming soak) followed by a controlled streaming run that simulates 80 concurrent sessions ramping to 120 for 90s. We will also run a short test that simulates burst behavior (600 tokens/sec) to observe queueing and GPU utilization.

Proposed preflight checklist (we'll send a runnable script but wanted to flag these items now):
- iperf3 5m run from app host -> Redwood egress (measure throughput + packet loss)
- traceroute + mtr for path stability (1m samples)
- MTU check (PMTU)
- 100-sample RTT distribution for small UDP/TCP packets
- Application-level small chunk throughput for SSE streaming test (measure inter-chunk delay)

For timing: if you can confirm the egress IPs and PoC window by Tue EOD (15 Jun), we can slot an internal engineering pair to run the PoC during the week of 6/21 and deliver the report within 48 hours of the run.

I'll loop Vivek for any deeper routing/peering questions — Vivek, can you review the diagram and call out any immediate red flags or preflow tests we should add?

Thanks — Jordan

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference VPN & Peering validation — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Jordan — reviewed the diagram quickly. A few notes from infra perspective: 
- F5 APM path looks straightforward; the TLS-inspection box is the largest single risk to tail latency variance. During PoC we'll capture per-packet timing before/after that hop.
- Recommend we request a short iperf run with TCP windowing and a separate UDP run to characterize jitter under NAT. If ACME can run iperf with parallel streams (4–8) that will exercise the concentrator well.
- If you can provide a small list of test client IPs (we can NAT them from our test pool), we'll ask NetOps to whitelist those egress IPs for the PoC window.

Operational asks for the PoC run:
1) Confirm two dedicated egress IPs and the CIDR if possible.
2) Provide one app host (or an IP we can schedule) to run iperf/traceroute; we will send the exact commands.
3) Share any firewall ACLs that could rewrite traffic or perform deep packet inspection.

I'll plan to join the PoC run remotely and can be on the 4-hour window. If NetOps confirms the 6/21 slot, I'll block time now.

— Vivek
